sentences.text: The Saffire investigations aimed to determine how rapidly a large-scale fire grows in low-gravity and to compare low-g flammability limits to normal gravity material flammability screening tests.

During microgravity fabric burns of SIBAL fabric (40.6 by 94 cm in air at about 21.5 percent O2 and 1 atm), concurrent-flow flame spread reached a steady rate of 1.8 mm/s in Saffire-I under a 20 cm/s duct flow.
In Saffire-III, under a 25 cm/s flow, the steady flame spread rate was measured at 2.3 mm/s.
By contrast, the same sample burns completely and the fire accelerates in 1 g normal gravity.

sentences.text: Smoke from overheated spacecraft materials in low gravity is sub-micron, with a substantial fraction of particles below 500 nm in SAME and most average sizes ranging from 200 to 400 nm in SAME-2.

In a microgravity environment without strong buoyancy-induced flows, smoke particle growth from pyrolyzing or smoldering sources leads to larger particles compared to those produced in 1g due to nucleation, condensation, and coagulation.
This change in size distribution and number density affects the response of smoke detectors and can possibly result in some detectors failing to produce an alarm when exposed to this smoke.

sentences.text: Raising the oxygen concentration to hold breathing partial pressure at a lower total pressure makes a cabin more flammable, because fire responds to oxygen mole fraction rather than partial pressure.
